BackstoryDef.title: spear bearer
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] carried spears and water for the tribe's war band. [PAWN_pronoun] watched every fight from the edge of the field and practiced what [PAWN_pronoun] saw until the warriors let [PAWN_objective] stand in the line.

BackstoryDef.title: wolf runner
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] ran with the tribe's hunting pack as soon as [PAWN_pronoun] was old enough to keep up. [PAWN_pronoun] learned to read tracks, to stay downwind, and to put an arrow where it counted.

BackstoryDef.title: raid orphan
BackstoryDef.description: Raiders burned [PAWN_nameDef]'s village and killed [PAWN_possessive] parents. The survivors raised [PAWN_objective] together, and [PAWN_pronoun] grew up watching families trade blame and blood over what had been lost.

BackstoryDef.title: chief's heir
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was the eldest child of a chief. From the day [PAWN_pronoun] could walk, [PAWN_pronoun] sat at the council fire, listened to the elders argue, and trained with the warriors who would one day follow [PAWN_objective].

BackstoryDef.title: war chief
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] led the tribe's warriors through years of raids and feuds. [PAWN_pronoun] fought at the front of every battle, and the tribe chose [PAWN_objective] as chief because no one else had brought so many of them home alive.

BackstoryDef.title: hunt master
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] fed the tribe through the hardest winters anyone could remember. [PAWN_pronoun] led the great hunts, chose where the tribe would camp, and became its chief when the old one could no longer keep pace.

BackstoryDef.title: oath keeper
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] settled blood feuds between families and held each side to its word. When words failed, [PAWN_pronoun] settled the matter with a blade. The tribe trusted [PAWN_possessive] judgment enough to make [PAWN_objective] chief.

BackstoryDef.title: clan unifier
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] brought several quarrelling clans under one banner through marriage pacts, gifts, and a few short wars. [PAWN_pronoun] rules them now and rides out with the war band whenever one of them is threatened.
